items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: Me and Caffrey was the only one on the roof garden that didn't read in the band. Caffrey and I, the only one.

ctx.x: Would Foster have any regular men or anything? No, just pick up men.

Pick up guys, yeah. I ain't never heard of this brass band play. They say he had brass band go out there and play fields and parades and whatever. Me and Caffrey was the only one on the roof garden that didn't read in the band. Caffrey and I, the only one. He played some fine music. You know he had to teach to play potent peasant? But he had to rehearse for that with me and Caffrey, you know, see, different movements. Mm-hmm.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: And Lil' Caffrey, Darius Boyd on the guitar.

ctx.x: How was Manuel Perez? Some people talk like he was the greatest of ever, and others say that he wasn't such a hot trumpet player, just a note reader, and that he really couldn't think anything. How did you like him? What did he sound like? He was a legitimate trumpet player.

Much more legitimate. Yeah, yeah. He wasn't a hot trumpet player, not a jazz trumpet player like of today. That's right, strictly music. That's right, a legitimate trumpet player. Did he have a big tone or? Nice tone, kind of nice tone. But it wasn't a fine tone, you know. It was more of a brass band tone, you see. Yeah. Kind of rough, you know. Loud, high notes. Notes didn't come too high, you see. Fine musician. Yeah, that's what I've heard. Yeah, I worked with him on the Roof Garden, Maurice Durand and I, and…
Who was the alto player? Was it before Tad's or after him?

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-02-03
items.q: Now he was a fine solo man, little Caffrey.

ctx.x: Well, at that time, you say you'd have your ensemble first. About how many choruses ensemble?

Oh, they'd play about three. About three on the choruses. Yeah, all together. Yeah, you see they play all. Now my idea, when they first started to play them solos, when they got the banjos? Yeah, the banjos. Yeah, you see. That guy was playing with us, Buddy Malady, you see, was playing with Buddy. When I was playing with Buddy, the guy was playing with Sam. Caffrey was playing on the roof guard. Now he was a fine solo man, little Caffrey. Fine. He couldn't read it, but I wish he had to get the banjo he would play.
And that was after you came back.
